units.title: Hannah
units.subtitle: A woman's prayer, and the rules of prayer

lessons.title: Hannah (1): A rival and a husband
lessons.check_note: Bava Batra 16a, Rosh Hashanah 11a, Megillah 31a read on Sefaria 11/12. English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive. CHECK: Mishkan HaNefesh / CBB read Hannah as the Rosh Hashanah haftarah (and on which day).

cards.title: Year after year
cards.body: Every year Elkanah and his family go up to **the House of GOD**. His wife Peninnah has children. His wife **Hannah** has none, and every year it hurts again.

cards.q: In one view in the Talmud, Peninnah taunted Hannah for the sake of Heaven.
cards.why: Rabbi Levi: she upset Hannah "in order to motivate her to pray."

cards.gloss: "her rival, to make her miserable, would taunt her" (1:6).

cards.title: For the sake of Heaven?
cards.body: **Rabbi Levi**: both Satan, who accused Job, and **Peninnah** acted for the sake of Heaven. Peninnah upset Hannah "in order to motivate her to pray." The Talmud adds that when this was taught, Satan came and **kissed the teacher's feet** in gratitude.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Levi, why did Peninnah taunt Hannah?
choices: To move her to pray
To make Elkanah send her away
Out of plain jealousy
cards.why: Rabbi Levi reads even the taunting as aimed at **prayer**.
wrong_why: Rabbi Levi reads her more generously.

cards.he: הֲלוֹא אָֽנֹכִי טוֹב לָךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָה בָּנִֽים׃
cards.gloss: "Am I not more devoted to you than ten sons?" (1:8). Elkanah answers her grief with **his love**.

cards.title: Remembered on Rosh Hashanah
cards.body: The Talmud teaches that on Rosh Hashanah, **Sarah, Rachel and Hannah** were remembered by God and conceived sons. **Rabbi Elazar** links the word **remembered** in Hannah's story (1:19) to the Rosh Hashanah verse "memorial proclaimed with the blast of a shofar" (Leviticus 23:24).

cards.q: Which women does the Talmud say were remembered on Rosh Hashanah?
choices: Sarah, Rachel and Hannah
Miriam, Deborah and Hannah
Ruth, Esther and Hannah
cards.why: Three women who waited for a child: **Sarah, Rachel and Hannah**.

cards.title: Read on Rosh Hashanah
cards.body: So the Talmud names Hannah's story, **1 Samuel 1:1 to 2:10**, as a haftarah for Rosh Hashanah, because she too was blessed with a child on that day.

cards.prompt: Peninnah's taunts and Elkanah's love both miss what Hannah needs. When have you felt unseen by people close to you?

points: Rabbi Levi: Peninnah meant to **move her to pray**.
"**Am I not more devoted to you than ten sons?**"
Remembered on **Rosh Hashanah**, read on Rosh Hashanah.

lessons.title: Hannah (2): Only her lips moved
lessons.check_note: Berakhot 31a-b and Zohar Vayigash 10:99 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12.

cards.title: The priest is watching
cards.body: Hannah rises and prays before GOD. **Eli the priest** watches her mouth, and he gets it wrong.

cards.q: Which rule for the Amidah does the Talmud learn from Hannah?
choices: Say the words with your lips, but quietly
Pray only inside the Temple
Pray aloud so others can answer amen
Pray standing on one foot
cards.why: Her lips moved, and **her voice could not be heard** (1:13).

cards.he: וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל־לִבָּהּ רַק שְׂפָתֶיהָ נָּעוֹת וְקוֹלָהּ לֹא יִשָּׁמֵעַ
cards.gloss: "Hannah was praying in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard" (1:13).

cards.title: Laws from one verse
cards.body: **Rav Hamnuna** draws laws of prayer from this verse. **In her heart**: focus your heart on your prayer. **Only her lips moved**: say the words with your lips, not only in your mind. **Her voice could not be heard**: do not raise your voice in the Amidah. **Eli thought she was drunk**: a drunk person may not pray.

cards.q: What does Rav Hamnuna learn from "only her lips moved"?
choices: Say the words with your lips, not only in your heart
Pray as quickly as you can
Never pray when you are sad
cards.why: Prayer is **spoken**, even when it is silent.

cards.body: These are the rules for the **Amidah**, the standing prayer, which begins with **Avot**: said quietly, with the lips, and with the heart.

cards.title: The voice that cannot be heard
cards.body: The **Zohar** says true prayer is "another voice attached to the voice which is heard." So a person should pray with the voice no one else hears, **like Hannah**, whose voice could not be heard.

cards.gloss: "I have been pouring out my heart to GOD" (1:15).

cards.title: Not a master here
cards.body: On "Oh no, my lord!", one sage says Hannah was hinting: in this matter **you are not a master**, and the Divine Spirit is not on you, since you suspect me falsely. **Rabbi Elazar** learns two more rules: someone wrongly suspected should **say so** and clear her name, and someone who suspected wrongly must **make peace and bless**, as Eli does next.

cards.q: What does Rabbi Elazar learn from Eli's "Then go in peace"?
choices: Whoever wrongly suspects someone must make peace and bless them
Priests are never wrong
Never pray in a public place
cards.why: Eli was wrong, and he **blesses** her.
wrong_why: The Talmud says Eli was wrong here.

cards.prompt: To the priest, Hannah's prayer looked like drunkenness. What does your most honest prayer look like from the outside?

points: "**Only her lips moved**, but her voice could not be heard" (1:13).
Rav Hamnuna: **heart, lips, quiet**, and never drunk.
Eli was wrong, so he **blesses** her (Berakhot 31b).

lessons.title: Hannah (3): God of Hosts
lessons.check_note: Berakhot 31b and Zohar Toldot 3:20 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12. Rabbi's-teaching card: the connection is mine; check with Jamie.

cards.title: A vow
cards.body: Weeping, Hannah makes **a vow**: if God gives her a child, she will give the child back to God.

cards.q: According to the Talmud, Hannah was the first person ever to call God "Lord of Hosts."
cards.why: Rabbi Elazar: no one, since Creation, until Hannah.

cards.title: The first to say it
cards.body: **Rabbi Elazar**: from the day God created the world, no one called God **Lord of Hosts** until Hannah. Her argument: of all the hosts upon hosts You created, is it so hard for You to give me **one son**?

cards.q: In Berakhot 31b, why does Hannah call God "Lord of Hosts"?
choices: Among all the hosts God made, one son should not be hard to give
It was the Temple's usual name for God
Eli taught it to her
cards.why: **Hosts upon hosts**, and she asks for one child.
wrong_why: The Talmud says no one had used it before her.

cards.gloss: "she prayed to GOD" (1:10). The Hebrew preposition here is unusual: **upon** or **onto** God, and the Talmud notices it.

cards.title: Speaking boldly upward
cards.body: **Rabbi Elazar**: "Hannah spoke impertinently toward God on High," since the verse says she prayed **onto** God, not to God. He also reads her doubled "if You will look" as a dare: if You look now, good; if not, **You will see** anyway, and she tells God how she will hold God to the Torah's own promise.

cards.title: Above the stars
cards.body: The **Zohar** reads the same word another way: Hannah's prayer went **above** ordinary fate. Like Isaac's prayer for Rebekah, it rose "above the planetary influences."

cards.q: How does Rabbi Elazar read Hannah praying "onto" God?
choices: She spoke boldly, even impertinently, toward Heaven
She prayed on a rooftop
She prayed on someone else's behalf
cards.why: Hannah does not only plead; she **argues**.

cards.title: A people growing up
cards.body: Your rabbi reads the Torah as a people **growing up**: from a child's hero-God, through a strained and complicated relationship, toward God present in our own choices. Hannah is a grown-up's prayer: no priest needed, her own words, even **arguing with God**. On the same page of Talmud, Rabbi Akiva says, "The Torah spoke in the language of men."

src.ref: Teaching from Jamie's rabbi (oral, as Jamie retold it); Berakhot 31b
src.note: connection to Hannah is mine; check with Jamie

cards.gloss: "I, in turn, hereby lend him to GOD" (1:28). **Asked** (שָׁאַלְתִּי, 1:27) and **lent** (הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ) come from the same root.

cards.title: For this boy I prayed
cards.body: The Talmud tells a story behind 1:25-27. Young **Samuel** ruled, correctly, that anyone may slaughter an offering, not only a priest. But he ruled **in front of his teacher**, Eli, who said that deserved death. Hannah cried out: "I am the woman who stood here with you." Eli offered to pray for a greater son. She answered: for **this** boy I prayed, and I want no other.

cards.prompt: Hannah bargains, dares, and argues with God, and the Talmud learns its rules of prayer from her. Is there something you would only say to God boldly?

points: Hannah is the first to say **Lord of Hosts** (Berakhot 31b).
She prays **onto** God: boldly, even impertinently.

lessons.title: Hannah (4): My heart exults
lessons.check_note: Megillah 14a and Berakhot 29a read on Sefaria 11/12. CHECK: how Mishkan HaNefesh treats the nine-blessing Musaf (Reform practice may differ).

cards.title: A song
cards.body: Samuel is born, weaned, and brought to serve at the House of GOD. Then Hannah prays again, this time **a song**.

cards.q: The Talmud links the nine blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf Amidah to what?
choices: The nine mentions of God's name in Hannah's prayer
Nine months of pregnancy
Nine shofar blasts
Nine years Hannah waited
cards.why: Rabbi Yitzchak of Kartignin, in Berakhot 29a.

cards.gloss: "I have triumphed through GOD" (2:1). The Talmud reads the Hebrew image word by word: my **horn** is exalted.

cards.title: A prophetess
cards.body: The Talmud counts **seven prophetesses**: Sarah, Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, Abigail, Huldah and Esther. Hannah's proof is the **horn**: she said my horn, not my pitcher. David and Solomon were anointed from a horn and their kingship lasted; Saul and Jehu were anointed from a pitcher and theirs did not. Hannah **foresaw** it.

cards.q: Why does Megillah 14a call Hannah a prophetess?
choices: Her "horn" foresaw which anointed kings would last
She heard angels in Shiloh
Eli named her one
cards.why: **Horn**, not pitcher: her song looks ahead to David.

cards.title: No artist like our God
cards.body: On "There is no rock like our God" (2:2), the Talmud reads **rock** as **artist**. A person paints a form on a wall but cannot give it breath. God forms a child **inside its mother** and gives it breath and a soul. Fitting words from Hannah.
Every Amidah's **G'vurot** praises God in the same words: מֶלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה.

cards.title: Nine blessings
cards.body: **Rabbi Yitzchak of Kartignin**: the nine blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf prayer correspond to the **nine mentions of God's name** in Hannah's prayer. The reason: on Rosh Hashanah, Sarah, Rachel and **Hannah** were remembered.

cards.q: According to Berakhot 29a, why does Hannah's prayer shape the Rosh Hashanah Musaf?
choices: She was remembered on Rosh Hashanah
She wrote the Musaf prayer
She prayed in the Temple on Yom Kippur
cards.why: Remembered on Rosh Hashanah, so her prayer gives the day its **nine blessings**.

cards.he: מֵקִים מֵעָפָר דָּל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן
cards.gloss: "Raising the poor from the dust, Lifting up the needy from the dunghill" (2:8). The song turns the world **upside down**, as Hannah's own life was turned.

cards.prompt: Hannah's song is full of reversals: the poor raised, the mighty brought low. Where have you seen a reversal you once could not imagine?

points: Megillah 14a: Hannah, **a prophetess**: horn, not pitcher.
"**GOD deals death and gives life**": the G'vurot.
Berakhot 29a: **nine blessings** of Rosh Hashanah Musaf.
